alalal-e17276-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 3: whether the power of sinning is one or many.
concepts: unity of the power of sinning

alalal-e17276-d1e113.summary: States the third question: whether the power of sinning is one or many.
concepts: unity of the power of sinning

alalal-e17276-d1e120.summary: Argument for many: evil is done by speaking, walking, thinking, willing, choosing and many other actions that cannot be reduced to one power.

alalal-e17276-d1e139.summary: Sed contra: Augustine says that in every evil the will alone is blamed, so the will alone is the power of sinning.

alalal-e17276-d1e150.summary: Second sed contra: it was shown earlier that the act of the natural power of will, and not of other powers, is called evil.

alalal-e17276-d1e161.summary: Solution: the power that executes sin is manifold in a human being, but the power that commands sin is one only, the will.
claims: The will alone commands sin, though many powers execute it.

alalal-e17276-d1e179.summary: Refers back to the earlier distinction of how sin is differently in reason, free choice, will and other powers, which also applies here.
concepts: sin in reason, free choice and will

alalal-e17276.summary: Article 3 asks whether the power of sinning is one or many, given that sin is committed through speaking, walking, thinking and willing, while Augustine blames the will alone. Albert distinguishes the powers that execute sin, which are many, from the power that commands it, which is the will alone. He refers back to the earlier account of how sin is differently present in reason, free choice, will and the other powers.
claims: The power that commands sin is one, the will, while the powers that execute sin are many.
